versions.changelog: - No impact to users; this is a minor internal cleanup

- Updated scan instructions to require a globally installed `clawvet` CLI, removing `npx` usage for increased security.
- Clarified that the CLI is static and offline; AI/semantic analysis now runs only via the hosted API.
- Strengthened installation policy: block on clear evidence of hidden or fetched code regardless of grade; with `--strict`, block on any inspection gap.
- Expanded explanations on managing global installs, registry attestation, and safe automatic updates.
- Removed the file: skill-card.md.
- No user-facing changes included in this version.
- Updated installation instructions in SKILL.md to use a global install for policy config instead of npx, clarifying limitations with npx and symlinked paths.
- Tells the agent that `clawvet gate --print-config` exists, so it can set up automatic install-time scanning instead of only scanning on request.
- policy is now gate
- Adds the clawvet policy subcommand, an OpenClaw security.installPolicy hook that scans a staged skill before the install completes and returns allow, warn or block.

- Docs only patch
- Changed requirements: replaced npx with npm and removed Bash from allowed tools.
- Expanded and clarified instructions for acting on scan results and reporting verdicts.
False-positive repairs: vendor installer allowlist, path traversal code-only, taint requires executable context (0.11.1)

Static detection now catches real-world malicious skills. On a 500-skill
benchmark of real ClawHub and ClawHavoc skills, recall went from 0.00 to 0.96
and F1 from 0.00 to 0.83, with no API key and no AI pass.

Two co-occurrence rules did most of it. "Install a prerequisite" plus "run this
command" is now a single high finding, the pattern used to run code that isn't
in the skill. A credential read plus an outbound send is now a single critical
finding.

Also fixed: shell variables a skill assigns itself were reported as undeclared
env vars, the credential rule matched process.env and the plain word
"credentials", and incomplete frontmatter could push a clean skill over the
warning line on its own.

Scoring is context-aware now. Repeated hits of the same rule no longer stack linearly, and a dual-use capability (reading a credential file, docker exec, installing a cron job) is downweighted when the skill has no way to send data out or run remote code. On the benchmark this cuts the false-positive rate from 0.22 to 0.08 with no loss of recall.

Also fixes a crash when frontmatter lists requires.bins or requires.env as a single string instead of a list, and adds a 101-skill labeled benchmark with a stdlib eval harness (precision, recall, F1, MCC, ROC-AUC, bootstrap CIs).

clawvet 0.9.0 introduces prompt-injection hardening and signed releases.

- Skills can no longer bypass the AI analysis pass via prompt injection; override attempts are now reported as findings.
- Releases are now signed, enabling you to verify npm package provenance with npm audit signatures.
- Detection rules expanded to 57 patterns across 13 categories.
- Documentation now clarifies feedback reporting opens a prefilled GitHub issue.
- Removed the obsolete skill-card.md file.

- Updated version to 0.8.2 in SKILL.md.
- Removed skill-card.md file.
- No feature or functionality changes noted; this release appears to update documentation and remove an unused file.

v0.8.0: Cross-file payload assembly. Folder scans now assemble files referenced from SKILL.md (e.g. a setup.sh) before analysis, so a payload split across multiple files can no longer evade detection, the exact evasion technique used to slip malicious skills past registry static analysis. Also: semantic analysis now correctly parses LLM responses wrapped in markdown code fences. Includes the 0.7.x line: path-traversal hardening on --remote, audit grade summaries, shell-free CLI (execFile), and privacy-preserving (SHA-256 hashed) telemetry.

- Major refactor: removed 109 files, narrowing package scope to just the CLI scanner.
- Now includes only CLI code; all API/web/dashboard sources have been removed and are not part of the npm package.
- Folder scan now assembles and analyzes cross-file payloads referenced from SKILL.md (e.g. setup scripts).
- Improved semantic analysis: better parsing of large language model (LLM) outputs in markdown code fences.
- Hardened path handling and enhanced privacy for telemetry (names hashed, still opt-in).
- Audit results now include final grade summaries and flag high-risk skills for review.
- Documentation updated to clarify monorepo structure and what's included in the package.

clawvet v0.6.3

- Improved telemetry reliability: Telemetry events now await before exit, ensuring no loss of data.
- CI-friendly: Interactive prompts are skipped automatically in non-interactive (non-TTY) environments.
- Reduced feedback noise: Feedback prompt now shown every 5th scan, not every scan.
- Documentation and metadata updates to reflect linter/quality features and CI compatibility.
- Minor fixes and refinements to trust badge, caching, and feedback mechanisms.

clawvet v0.6.1

- The npm package is now fully stateless and offline—no database, authentication, or network required.
- Added trust badge generation: run npx clawvet badge ./skill/ to add a shields.io badge to your README.
- Introduced support for ban lists via .clawvetban files to block skills by name, author, or slug.
- Clarified monorepo structure: the npm package only ships the CLI; web dashboard components are separate and optional.
- Documentation updated for new features and improved clarity.

clawvet v0.6.0

- Added new "badge" command to CLI.
- Updated scan command and CLI index to support additional features.
- Enhanced pattern matching logic for improved threat detection.
- Expanded and improved integration, edge-case, and regex-safety test coverage.
- Dependency updates and internal refactoring for better maintainability.

clawvet v0.5.1

- Updated documentation for clarity and brevity, including improved usage instructions and analysis pass summary in SKILL.md.
- Minor metadata and description adjustments for better readability and consistency.
- Internal code and test updates to align with documentation changes.

clawvet v0.5.0 adds confidence scores, fix suggestions, and major performance improvements.

- Each finding now includes a confidence score, weighting risk to reduce false positives.
- Fix suggestions are displayed for every issue in both terminal and SARIF output.
- Content-hash caching enables near-instant scans for unchanged files.
- Added opt-in anonymous telemetry and the clawvet feedback command.
- Expanded documentation and included new security benchmarks for testing.
fix: edge cases — scan dir crash, audit --dir, watch exit code, typosquat false positive
Add homepage and repository URL to SKILL.md metadata
Fix CI, add ClawHub SKILL.md
Initial release: 6-pass security scanner with 54 detection patterns
